I will preserve the figure size and other styling, add a key for the hatching, and verify the plotted values against the table. print(table.tail(24).to_string(index=False)) source = Path("chart.py").read_text() start = source.index("sns.barplot(\n data=df_employment") end = source.index("plt.subplot(2, 2, 3)", start) replacement = '''from matplotlib.patches import Patch import numpy as np ax = plt.gca() bottom = np.zeros(len(countries)) sector_colors = {'Services': '#4e79a7', 'Industry': '#f28e2b', 'Agriculture': '#e15759'} for sector, employment in sectors.items(): for status, values in employment.items(): ax.bar(countries, values, bottom=bottom, color=sector_colors[sector], hatch='//' if status == 'Informal' else '', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5) bottom += np.asarray(values) plt.title("Employment Distribution by Sector (Formal vs Informal)") plt.xlabel("Country") plt.ylabel("Employment Share (%)") plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right') sector_legend = ax.legend( handles=[Patch(facecolor=color, label=sector) for sector, color in sector_colors.items()], title='Sector', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left') ax.add_artist(sector_legend) ax.legend(handles=[ Patch(facecolor='white', edgecolor='black', label='Formal'), Patch(facecolor='white', edgecolor='black', hatch='//', label='Informal') ], title='Employment Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 0.55), loc='upper left') ''' source = source[:start] + replacement + source[end:] source = source.replace("y='GDP per Capita (USD)',\n color='#59a14f'", "y='Unemployment Rate (%)',\n color='#59a14f'") source = source.replace("y='Unemployment Rate (%)',\n color='#b07aa1'", "y='GDP per Capita (USD)',\n color='#b07aa1'") Path("chart.py").write_text(source) exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec")) fig = plt.gcf() for ax in fig.axes: print(ax.get_title(), "ylim:", ax.get_ylim(), "bars:", len(ax.patches)) print("Table sectors:", table["Sector"].unique()) continue
